The token match is gone (namesToken and `commands` removed). Ids now come only from explicit argument positions (src/review/completion-gate.ts:216-231) and from the output of an opening command that ran alone (:295, :303-313). But namedBySession still matches the manifest's own `reviewId` (scanRoot :375-376 passes [head.reviewId, name]; pickPackage :393 passes candidate.id = head.reviewId). Review ids are predictable: date + mode + PR URL slug, e.g. this package's 2026-10-17-review-flow-github-com-mrciphersmith-keryx-pull-1045-r02. A PR can commit `.metaproject/reviews/<other-dir>/manifest.json` (draft, review-flow) whose reviewId is the id `keryx review start` will print. Once that id is named, the package is sessionNamed, and when it is newest it is chosen (:394), so the nudge repeats its blockers. Separately, :228 takes the first non-dash word as the positional id, which can be a flag's value (`readiness --flow 460 <id>` names `460`). Fix: match by package directory/basename only, or require head.reviewId === basename.

A closed manifest must now be named by this session to release the gate (src/review/completion-gate.ts:437-439), and the test at completion-gate.test.ts:144 pins the unnamed case. The closed entry's ids still include the attacker-controlled manifest reviewId (:370 `ids: [head.reviewId, name]`). A committed closed manifest whose reviewId equals the predictable id of the real package is therefore named. When its checkout mtime is later than the real package's last manifest write, it releases the gate (:439).

resolveDiffBases (src/review/coverage.ts:568-577) measures the recorded base and the default base (origin/main, main, origin/master, master) and keeps the wider diff, so `--base head~1` cannot shrink a PR when a default base resolves. The test at coverage.test.ts:1809 pins this. If no default branch resolves (a repo whose base is develop/trunk with no main/master ref), `fallback` is null (:571, :575), and the recorded base alone is measured, as before. That narrowing still holds there. The baseRefOid check suggested in round 2 was not adopted.

As r2-review-security-code-w1:SEC-R2-002: an unnamed closed manifest no longer releases the gate (completion-gate.ts:437). Naming can still come through the committed manifest's own predictable reviewId (:370).
